summary: Perampanel is a once-daily, bedtime oral antiseizure medication that noncompetitively antagonizes AMPA glutamate receptors. It is used for partial-onset seizures (monotherapy or adjunctive) and as adjunctive therapy for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures. It carries a boxed warning for serious psychiatric and behavioral reactions (aggression, hostility, homicidal ideation). It is a CYP3A4 substrate (strong inducers reduce levels) and requires slow titration; dose is capped in hepatic impairment.
indications: Treatment of partial-onset seizures with or without secondarily generalized seizures (monotherapy or adjunctive) in patients 4 years and older
Adjunctive therapy of primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients 12 years and older

moa: Noncompetitive antagonist of the ionotropic AMPA glutamate receptor on postsynaptic neurons, reducing glutamate-mediated excitatory neurotransmission and thereby suppressing seizure activity.

relative: Severe hepatic or severe renal impairment / hemodialysis

preg: Limited human data. Use during pregnancy only if benefit outweighs risk; may reduce efficacy of progestin-containing contraceptives at higher doses. Encourage enrollment in a pregnancy registry.
lact: Perampanel and metabolites are present in animal milk; presence in human milk uncertain. Consider developmental benefits of breastfeeding against potential risk to the infant.
renal: No adjustment for mild renal impairment; not recommended in severe renal impairment or patients on hemodialysis.
hepatic: Maximum 6 mg/day in mild and 4 mg/day in moderate hepatic impairment, with titration no more often than every 2 weeks; not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, oxcarbazepine, rifampin, St. John's wort) - markedly reduce perampanel levels; higher dose needed
CNS depressants and alcohol - additive sedation and increased anger/aggression
moderate: Progestin-containing contraceptives - perampanel 12 mg reduces levonorgestrel exposure; use additional non-hormonal contraception
CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole) - may modestly increase levels
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food delays and lowers peak concentration but does not change overall exposure.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - potentiates CNS depression and significantly increases anger, confusion, and aggression.
interactions.diagnostics: No routine therapeutic drug level monitoring; monitor clinically.

serious: Serious psychiatric/behavioral reactions (aggression, hostility, anger, homicidal ideation/threats)
Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

monitoring: Psychiatric and behavioral changes (aggression, hostility, mood) - especially during titration and at higher doses

pearls: Boxed warning for serious psychiatric/behavioral reactions - monitor closely during titration and at high doses

Schedule III controlled substance in the US
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin) substantially lower levels and require higher dosing

missed: If a single dose is missed, resume at the next scheduled dose; do not double up. If more than one dose is missed or therapy is interrupted for more than a few days, consult the prescriber - re-titration may be needed.
overdose: Limited experience. Overdose may cause altered mental status, agitation, aggression, and decreased consciousness. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care and monitor; perampanel is highly protein-bound so dialysis is unlikely to help. Given the long half-life, monitor for a prolonged period.
